paper.title_en: Recent results of Baryon electromagnetic form factors at BESIII
paper.abstract_en: Electromagnetic form factors (EMFFs) are fundamental observables for understanding baryon structure. At the BESIII experiment, the time-like EMFFs of various baryons have been systematically investigated. The proton EMFF ratio $|G_E/G_M|$ has been precisely determined, enabling the first extraction of the $|G_E|$ lineshape, while recent neutron EMFF measurements show remarkable improvements in precision over previous experiments. Taking advantage of the self-analyzing weak decays, the relative phases of the time-like EMFFs for $\Lambda$ and $\Sigma^+$ have been measured for the first time. This non-zero phase naturally induces a transverse polarization of the final state baryons, highlighting the importance of spin observables in probing baryon structure.
